title: Pompeii Wardrobe Opens After Almost 2,000 Years
paragraphs: Sealed for almost two thousand years, a wooden cupboard in Pompeii has finally given up its contents, and the picture it paints is refreshingly ordinary. The Archaeological Park of Pompeii announced the find in late October 2026. The piece of furniture stood in a house on the bustling Via dell'Abbondanza that has been tentatively associated with a man named Cornelius Maximus; although the facade was excavated in 1912, the rooms behind it have only now come under scrutiny.

Among the objects were a necklace of at least 24 miniature amulets in bone, glass paste, faience and rock crystal, depicting deities such as Mercury and Bes as well as tiny hands, feet, pine cones and grapes. Necklaces of this kind were hung on Roman children, which raises the possibility that it belonged to a child of the house or was kept by an adult as a keepsake. The cupboard also held 38 bronze coins, mostly from the reign of Nero, tweezers, a perfume bottle, an incense burner, and a wooden box of lead weights that points to someone engaged in commerce.

The temptation is to imagine a family fleeing in panic, leaving their treasured possessions behind, and researchers do consider that the owners may have left in haste. Yet the director, Gabriel Zuchtriegel, was careful to note that the occupants cannot be identified with certainty, and it is unclear whether they perished or escaped. His broader point, that Pompeii is “not just a place of great works of art,” is perhaps the finding's real value: humble objects restore the human dimension of the past.

questions.q: Why does the necklace invite two possible explanations?
questions.a: It is a type worn by Roman children, so it may have belonged to a child or been kept by an adult.

questions.q: What did the director caution against?
questions.a: Assuming the occupants' identity or fate with certainty.

questions.q: What does the writer see as the real value of the find?
questions.a: It restores the human dimension of the past through humble objects.
